stem.en: Which pair can NOT be overloaded methods in the same class?

options.en: int f(int a) and double f(int b)
int f(int a) and int f(double a)
int f(int a) and int f(int a, int b)
void f(char c) and void f(String s)

explanation.en: They differ only in return type; the parameter lists are the same.

stem.en: The parameters in the method header are called:

explanation.en: The values in the call are actual parameters (arguments).

stem.en: A method that changes the state of an object is called:

Assertion (A): A method void inc(int a) { a++; } cannot change the variable passed to it.
Reason (R): Java passes primitive arguments by value.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: The method works on a copy. R explains A.

stem.en: Which is true about a constructor?

options.en: It has the same name as the class and no return type
It is called with the dot operator

explanation.en: Constructors are named after the class and have no return type.

stem.en: If a class defines only Student(String n), what does new Student() do?

options.en: It sets the name to null

explanation.en: Java supplies a default constructor only when no constructor is written.

stem.en: In this.marks = marks;, this.marks refers to:

options.en: The instance variable of the current object

explanation.en: this.marks is the field; marks alone is the parameter that hides it.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): A call this(...) must be the first statement in a constructor.
Reason (R): An object must be fully initialised by one constructor before other statements use it.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Java requires constructor chaining to come first. R explains A.

options.en: Shared by all objects of the class

explanation.en: There is one copy per class.

stem.en: Which statement about a static method is correct?

options.en: It must be called on an object
It can directly use instance variables

explanation.en: A static method has no current object, so no this.

stem.en: The scope of a variable declared in the header of a for loop is:

explanation.en: for (int i = 0; …) makes i local to the loop.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Math.sqrt(16) is called without creating a Math object.
Reason (R): sqrt is a static method of the Math class.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Static methods are called on the class name. R explains A.
